name: Beef, Mushroom & Black Pepper Velouté
desc: Dark, peppery and intensely savoury — the current front-runner.
ing: 250 g cooked lean beef, roughly chopped
350 ml water, or enough to remain below MAX
method: Add beef, mushrooms, onion, garlic, stock, thyme, Worcestershire and water.
Run the Smooth programme.
Stir in the cream and black pepper.
Use Blend briefly for an ultra-silky finish; taste before adding salt.
science: High-quality protein plus iron, zinc and B vitamins from beef; mushrooms add savoury glutamates.
note: Use cooked beef only. The MAX line wins over any written liquid quantity.

name: Lamb, Roasted Pepper & Cumin Cream
desc: Rich lamb against sweet roasted pepper, cumin and smoked paprika.
ing: 180 g jarred roasted red peppers, drained
method: Add lamb, peppers, tomatoes, onion, garlic, cumin, paprika, stock and water.
Run Smooth.
Stir in cream and black pepper.
Blend briefly and season to taste.
science: Lamb supplies protein, iron and zinc; red pepper contributes vitamin C and carotenoids.
note: Keep the cumin warm and savoury rather than curry-like.

name: Duck, Shiitake & Five-Spice Cream
desc: Dark mushroom richness with duck and a very restrained five-spice note.
ing: 400 ml chicken stock, adjusted to MAX
method: Add duck, mushrooms, onion, garlic, stock, soy and five-spice.
Run Smooth.
Add cream and black pepper.
Blend briefly and adjust seasoning.
science: Duck gives richer flavour and more fat than chicken; mushrooms carry the umami load.
note: Five-spice should be barely identifiable.

name: Pea, Smoked Bacon & Black Pepper
desc: Thick, green and smoky without relying on potato.
method: Add peas, two-thirds of the bacon, onion, garlic, stock and water.
Run Smooth.
Add cream and black pepper, then Blend briefly.
Use the remaining bacon as topping if you want texture.
science: Peas provide fibre and plant protein; bacon brings smoke, salt and richness.
note: Frozen peas are ideal because there is effectively no waste.

name: Chorizo, Tomato & Smoked Paprika
desc: A dark, smoky tomato soup with cured chorizo doing the heavy lifting.
method: Add chorizo, tomatoes, pepper, onion, garlic, stock, water and paprika.
Run Smooth.
Add cream if using.
Blend briefly and season.
science: Chorizo adds protein and a lot of flavour, but also salt and saturated fat.
note: Use ready-to-eat cured chorizo rather than raw cooking chorizo.

name: Chicken, Sweetcorn, Ginger & Garlic
desc: A smooth, savoury chicken-and-sweetcorn soup with ginger warmth and plenty of garlic.
ing: 240 g cooked chicken breast, roughly chopped
method: Add chicken, sweetcorn, onion, garlic, ginger, stock and water.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add cream and plenty of black pepper.
Blend briefly, then taste before adding salt.
science: A high-protein soup with sweetcorn supplying carotenoids and chicken providing a substantial dose of complete protein.
note: Use cooked chicken only. Keep the ginger warm rather than dominant.

name: Chicken, Mushroom & Tarragon Cream
desc: Classic chicken-and-mushroom flavours made much deeper with tarragon, garlic and Parmesan.
method: Add chicken, mushrooms, onion, garlic, tarragon, stock and water.
Run Smooth.
Add cream, Parmesan and black pepper.
Blend briefly until completely silky.
science: Chicken supplies protein while mushrooms and Parmesan provide layered savouriness, letting the soup taste rich without potato.
note: Tarragon can take over quickly; ½ tsp dried is enough for the first batch.

name: Smoked Ham, Pea & Mature Cheddar
desc: A thick pea-and-ham soup pushed into proper cold-weather territory with mature Cheddar.
method: Add ham, peas, onion, garlic, stock and water.
Run Smooth.
Add Cheddar, cream and plenty of black pepper.
Blend briefly until the cheese is fully incorporated.
science: Peas add fibre and plant protein while ham and Cheddar bring substantial protein, salt and savoury flavour.
note: Taste before salting — smoked ham, stock and Cheddar may already be enough.

name: Turkey, Kale & Parmesan Cream
desc: A high-protein green soup that still tastes rich rather than worthy.
method: Add turkey, kale, cauliflower, onion, garlic, stock and water.
Run Smooth.
Add Parmesan, cream and black pepper.
Blend briefly until no green flecks remain.
science: Turkey gives a large serving of complete protein; kale contributes folate and carotenoids; cauliflower provides body without potato.
note: Remove tough kale stalks so the finished soup stays smooth.

name: Roast Pork, Apple & Sage Cream
desc: Savoury roast pork with a small amount of tart apple, sage and cream — more roast dinner than sweet soup.
ing: 1 small tart eating apple, about 100 g, cored and chopped
method: Add pork, apple, onion, garlic, sage, stock and water.
Run Smooth.
Add cream and generous black pepper.
Blend briefly and season to taste.
science: Pork supplies protein and B vitamins; the apple is deliberately modest and mainly provides aromatic contrast to the meat.
note: Use a tart apple and keep the quantity small so the soup stays savoury.

name: Beef, Roasted Pepper & Horseradish Cream
desc: Rich beef and roasted pepper with just enough horseradish to sharpen the background.
method: Add beef, pepper, onion, garlic, stock, water and smoked paprika.
Run Smooth.
Add cream, horseradish and black pepper.
Blend briefly and taste; the horseradish should remain subtle.
science: Beef supplies protein, iron and zinc; red pepper adds vitamin C and carotenoids.
note: Horseradish is deliberately low-profile to fit your preference.

name: Lamb, Tomato & Spinach Cumin Velouté
desc: Deep lamb, tomato and cumin with spinach folded into a completely smooth, rich soup.
method: Add lamb, tomatoes, spinach, onion, garlic, cumin, paprika, stock and water.
Run Smooth.
Add Greek yoghurt and black pepper.
Blend briefly until velvety.
science: Lamb contributes protein, iron and zinc; spinach adds folate and carotenoids.
note: This is meant to taste of lamb first, cumin second.

name: Duck, Mushroom & Port Velouté
desc: A dark, luxurious duck-and-mushroom soup with a small port note and plenty of black pepper.
method: Add duck, mushrooms, onion, garlic, stock, water and port.
Run Smooth.
Add cream and plenty of black pepper.
Blend briefly and season.
science: Duck provides protein and richness; mushrooms give the soup enough umami to support the sweeter wine note.
note: The port should read as background depth, not sweetness. If avoiding alcohol, replace with 1 tsp balsamic.

name: Duck, Roasted Garlic & Black Pepper Cream
desc: A deliberately simple duck soup built around garlic, pepper and a rich creamy finish.
method: Add duck, mushrooms, onion, garlic, stock, water and Worcestershire sauce.
Run Smooth.
Add cream and black pepper.
Blend briefly and adjust seasoning.
science: A protein-rich soup whose flavour comes mainly from duck, garlic, pepper and mushroom rather than starch.
note: This completes a practical three-recipe duck week alongside the five-spice version.

name: Garlic Chicken, Parmesan & Sweetcorn Roast-Dinner Cream
desc: Roast-chicken comfort translated into a silky, potato-free soup.
ing: 240 g cooked chicken breast, roughly chopped
340 ml water, or enough to remain below MAX
method: Add 240 g cooked chicken breast, 200 g sweetcorn, ½ medium onion, 5 garlic cloves, ½ tsp dried thyme, 1 chicken stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 30 g parmesan, 60 ml double cream, 1 tsp worcestershire sauce, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Chicken provides a large serving of complete protein; sweetcorn contributes carotenoids while Parmesan adds calcium and savoury depth.
note: Use cooked chicken only. The garlic is deliberately generous.

name: Ham, Pea & Mustard Cream
desc: Smoked ham and pea with only a quiet English-mustard background.
method: Add 180 g cooked smoked ham, 330 g frozen peas, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 chicken stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 60 ml double cream, ¼ tsp english mustard, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Peas add fibre and plant protein while ham contributes complete protein; mustard is present for balance, not heat.
note: Taste before adding salt: ham and stock are already salty.

name: Ham, Leek & Cheddar Cream
desc: A leek-and-ham comfort soup with mature Cheddar instead of a potato base.
method: Add 180 g cooked ham, 220 g leek, 120 g cauliflower florets, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 chicken stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 60 g mature cheddar, 50 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Ham and Cheddar provide substantial protein; cauliflower gives body without making the soup taste of potato.
note: Wash the leek particularly well.

name: Pork, Mushroom & Miso Velouté
desc: Tonjiru-adjacent pork and mushroom with miso, but richer and more velvety.
method: Add 210 g cooked pork, 250 g chestnut mushrooms, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, 10 g ginger and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 20 g white or awase miso, 1 tsp light soy sauce, ½ tsp toasted sesame oil, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Pork supplies protein and B vitamins; mushroom, miso and soy layer complementary sources of umami.
note: Add the miso after cooking so its flavour stays cleaner.

name: Chicken, Almond & Roasted-Garlic Cauliflower
desc: Creamy chicken thickened with cauliflower and almond rather than potato.
method: Add 230 g cooked chicken, 280 g cauliflower florets, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, 1 chicken stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 30 g smooth almond butter, 60 g greek yoghurt, pinch of nutmeg, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Chicken delivers complete protein; almonds add unsaturated fat and vitamin E while cauliflower supplies vitamin C.
note: Smooth almond butter gives a more reliable texture than whole nuts.

name: Turkey, Mushroom & Parmesan Cream
desc: Lean turkey made properly comforting with mushroom, Parmesan and black pepper.
method: Add 240 g cooked turkey, 240 g chestnut mushrooms, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, 1 chicken stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 30 g parmesan, 50 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Turkey is a very protein-dense base; mushrooms and Parmesan make the soup taste far richer than the fat content suggests.
note: Excellent for using leftover roast turkey.

name: Beef, Onion & Gruyère Velouté
desc: French-onion flavour architecture without pretending the soup maker caramelises onions.
method: Add 240 g cooked lean beef, 220 g onion, 150 g chestnut mushrooms, 4 garlic cloves, 1 beef stock cube, 350 ml water, 1 tsp worcestershire sauce and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 45 g gruyère, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Beef provides protein, iron and zinc; Gruyère and Worcestershire compensate for the lack of true onion caramelisation.
note: This is French-onion-inspired, not a substitute for properly caramelised onion soup.

name: Lamb, Mushroom & Rosemary Cream
desc: Earthy mushroom, rosemary and garlic wrapped around a rich lamb base.
method: Add 220 g cooked lamb, 230 g chestnut mushrooms, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, ½ tsp dried rosemary, 1 stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 60 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Lamb contributes protein, iron and zinc; mushrooms intensify the savoury profile.
note: Rosemary is potent: keep it restrained.

name: Chorizo, Roasted Pepper & Manchego
desc: Smoky cured chorizo, pepper and nutty Manchego in a dense Spanish-style soup.
ing: 300 g jarred roasted red pepper, drained
method: Add 110 g ready-to-eat cured chorizo, 300 g jarred roasted red pepper, 200 g chopped tomatoes, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves, ½ tsp smoked paprika and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 40 g manchego, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Chorizo and Manchego bring protein and a great deal of flavour; peppers and tomatoes provide carotenoids.
note: Use cured ready-to-eat chorizo, not raw cooking chorizo.

name: Pork, Fennel & Parmesan Cream
desc: Pork with aromatic fennel, garlic and Parmesan — sausage-shop flavours without the sausage texture.
method: Add 210 g cooked pork, 180 g fennel bulb, 120 g cauliflower florets, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, 1 chicken stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 30 g parmesan, 50 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Pork supplies protein and B vitamins; fennel gives aromatic lift while cauliflower supplies body.
note: If you dislike aniseed, skip this one: fennel is deliberately noticeable.

name: Chicken, Roasted Pepper & Feta Paprika Cream
desc: Mediterranean chicken, feta and roasted pepper with a smoky paprika backbone.
method: Add 230 g cooked chicken, 260 g roasted red peppers, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, ½ tsp smoked paprika, 1 chicken stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 70 g feta, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Chicken gives complete protein; red pepper contributes vitamin C and carotenoids; feta adds calcium and salt.
note: Feta supplies enough acidity that lemon is unnecessary.
